references.text: Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is a repeated action in burnt offering rituals, symbolizing identification with the sacrifice.
Aaron's sons shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar, the same practice as in the peace offering ritual.
Describes the same ritual actions of laying on of hands, slaughter, and blood sprinkling for a peace offering from the herd.
Parallel description of the peace offering ritual when the sacrifice is a lamb, with the same elements of laying on of hands and slaughter before the tent of meeting.
Laying on of hands and slaughter of the sin offering follow the same pattern as the peace offering.
The sin offering ritual includes laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal and slaughter at the place of burnt offering.
At the consecration of the tabernacle, Aaron and his sons were to lay their hands on the head of the bull, the same ritual action.
The blood was to be sprinkled around on the altar, as in the peace offering ritual.
Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
Emphasizes the theology that the sacrifice must take place directly 'before the face of the Lord' as the basis for atonement.
Historical fulfillment of the ritual procedure described in the law.
Direct narrative exemplification of the peace offering ritual described in the law.
